fieldMarks: Resembles a female mallard but with a much darker body and a paler gray head.
Drake has a yellow bill; hen's bill is duller.
Speculum dark purple without the bold white borders of a mallard.
In flight, white underwings contrast strongly with the dark body.
behavior: Dabbles, up-ends and grazes; freshwater birds eat mostly seeds, leaves and roots, coastal birds take mussels, clams, snails and small crustaceans.
Call is a typical duck quack.
Fall migration is often late, as waters freeze or food runs out; northern breeders migrate far, coastal birds only short distances.
Frequently hybridizes with mallards, especially in the Northeast.
habitat: Marshes, bays, estuaries, ponds, rivers and lakes; uses salt marsh more than most dabblers, and also tree-lined ponds and wooded swamps.
range: Eastern Canada, the Great Lakes and the Atlantic coast from New England through the Mid-Atlantic to the Southeast and Florida. Replaces the mallard in the Maritime provinces.

lookalikes.name: Mallard
lookalikes.howToTell: Mallard hens are lighter mottled brown with an orange-and-black bill and a blue speculum bordered in white; black ducks are darker with a dark purple speculum lacking bold white edges.
